citation: Bucol, A. A., & Carumbana, E. E. (2010). Checklist of fishes found in the fresh and brackish waters of Negros and Siquijor, Philippines. Asian Journal of Biodiversity, 1(1), 91–125. https://doi.org/10.7828/ajob.v1i1.104

accessReview.bibliographicAndFullTextAccess: Correction to the initial review: an official Asian Journal of Biodiversity article page and publisher-hosted PDF were located and accessed; an author-uploaded ResearchGate copy is also available. This confirms public access to the article, not permission to reuse or redistribute its checklist.

waterbodiesAndAreas: Negros Island fresh and brackish waters (broad compilation)
Siquijor Island fresh and brackish waters (broad compilation)
Siaton River, Negros Oriental (extensive author collection, May 2004–October 2005, four stations)
Bago River, Negros Occidental (compiled literature and small-scale collections; approximate source coordinate envelope)
Pagatban River, Negros Oriental (ongoing collection noted by authors; not a complete survey in this checklist)
evidenceScope.sourceReportedScope: The article reports a tentative compiled list of 89 species in 45 families across fresh and brackish waters of Negros and Siquijor. It combines published literature and collections rather than one contemporaneous island-wide survey.
evidenceScope.taxonomyAndEcologyContext: The source classifies fish as primary freshwater, secondary freshwater, migratory, sporadic visitor or brackish-water species. These are source-era interpretations requiring independent review.
evidenceScope.samplingDatesAndLocalitySpecificCoverage: Siaton collection dates and station count are explicit. The broad checklist also references older literature, 2006–2010 collections, Bago River, Siquijor and an ongoing Pagatban collection; it is not a current, complete waterbody inventory.

decision.use: Broad historical source-discovery lead only; do not use the aggregate 89 as an app checklist or region-completion count.
decision.reason: The authors explicitly call their list tentative, compile multiple years and locations, use 2010-era taxonomy, and provide no verified reuse license. Broad island evidence cannot be expanded into per-waterbody or current-presence rows.

nextActions: Prefer accessible, dated primary waterbody studies for site-level evidence; use this checklist only to discover underlying sources.
For any future candidate, record its exact cited locality, date, taxon rank, collection or voucher basis, and source spelling from the underlying primary source.
Verify item-specific reuse terms before transcribing or redistributing the checklist or annotations; the official publisher-hosted copy resolves the access gap only.
Keep fresh, brackish, migratory and marine-visitor evidence separate; do not infer habitat suitability, current presence, diet, catchability, rules or safety.
limitations: The publisher-hosted PDF is accessible, but no item-specific reuse license was verified; access is not publication approval.
The paper calls the 89-species list tentative and notes that ongoing Pagatban collection may add species.
Taxonomy and ecological categories have not been reconciled against current fish authorities or waterbody-specific events.
No list, species assertion, abundance, geometry or public-app row is created by this review.
